text: Antimicrobial resistance in Salmonella enterica is driven by plasmid-borne genes. Resistance determinants spread between isolates by conjugative transfer. Surveillance of resistant isolates relies on serotyping and whole genome sequencing. The blaCTX-M family confers extended spectrum beta-lactamase activity in many enteric bacteria. Fluoroquinolone resistance arises from point mutations in gyrase and topoisomerase genes. Monitoring resistant Salmonella in poultry production remains a public health priority for食品 safety programmes worldwide. Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy within chloroplast thylakoid membranes. Photosystem II oxidises water and releases molecular oxygen as a by-product. Electrons pass along the transport chain to plastoquinone and the cytochrome complex. The proton gradient established across the membrane drives ATP synthase. Carbon fixation proceeds through the Calvin cycle using ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase. Light harvesting complexes tune their antenna size to the prevailing irradiance of the leaf canopy environment. Seismic waves propagate through the Earth interior at velocities set by density and elastic moduli. Primary waves are compressional and arrive first at a recording station. Secondary waves are transverse and cannot travel through the liquid outer core. The shadow zone observed between certain epicentral distances established the existence of that core. Travel time curves let analysts locate hypocentres from arrival differences. Modern broadband networks record ground motion continuously for tomographic inversion of mantle structure.
